prompt.context: Our client, Classic Bookstore (CB), is a traditional bookstore chain in Spain, specialized in non-technical books. CB's revenue has stagnated for the past 3 years, with a stable and loyal customer base. Now, as part of its new growth strategy, CB is considering whether to enter the electronic books market. The client is considering selling a CB-branded reading device and developing a website to sell e-books for it.
prompt.question: Our client has asked us to analyze this opportunity and provide a recommendation on whether to enter the electronic books market.

clarifying_info.a: CB only sells to customers through physical stores; no online business is available.
CB has stores in the largest cities in Spain.
CB has 3 types: Avid Readers (2 books/month), Occasional Readers (1 book every 2 months), and Rare Readers (1 book every 6 months).

clarifying_info.q: What is the state of the physical book market?
clarifying_info.a: The non-technical physical book market in Spain has been stagnated for the past 3 years.

clarifying_info.q: What is the cost of the e-reader device?
clarifying_info.a: CB has reached an agreement with an e-Reader manufacturer in China. Total cost per device would be 60€. These devices can only support e-books sold on CB's new website.

clarifying_info.q: What growth rate is the client targeting?
clarifying_info.a: CB has no specific growth rate in mind and is open to suggestions.

exhibits.title: Non-Technical Books Market in Spain
exhibits.shows: Two pie charts showing market share breakdown: one for the e-books market in Spain and one for the paper books market in Spain, plus key market metrics for each segment.

exhibits.title: Electronic Readers Comparison
exhibits.shows: Comparison table of four e-reader devices across price, cost, accepted formats, storage capacity, and extra features.

exhibits.title: CB's Customers Information
exhibits.shows: Breakdown of CB's 390,000 total customers by reader type, what they value most about CB, and willingness to switch to an electronic reader by segment.

framework: Market Opportunity: Estimate the size of the non-technical book market in Spain (both paper and e-books); assess market growth rates and competitive landscape
Potential Market Share: Identify competitors in the e-book space; estimate CB's achievable market share given brand recognition and existing customer base
Potential Profitability: Calculate expected revenues (e-books + e-reader sales) vs. costs (website investment, general expenses, cannibalization); determine payback period and ROI

Capabilities & Risks: Assess strategic alignment with CB's existing model; evaluate financial capability; identify cannibalization risk from existing paper book customers; consider lack of e-commerce know-how

questions.prompt: Estimate the size of the non-technical books market in Spain (paper and e-books).
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a bottom-up estimate starting from Spain's population, narrow to the reading-age cohort (15-80), apply a book-buying penetration rate, segment by reader type, then split paper vs. e-book volumes and apply average prices. Strong candidates show clear assumptions at each step.

math.setup: Spain population = 45M. Age 0-20 = 25% = 11.25M; ages 15-20 ≈ 2.8M. Ages 21-40 = 11.25M, 41-60 = 11.25M, 61-80 = 11.25M. Target (15-80) = 36.5M. 60% buy books → 22M buyers. Split: 2M Avid (12 books/yr), 5M Occasional (6 books/yr), 15M Rare (2 books/yr).
math.answer: Paper market ≈ 1,170M€ (0% growth); e-book market ≈ 48M€ (5% annual growth). Total non-technical books market ≈ 1,220M€.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, determine the recommended price for the CB e-Reader and justify the choice.
questions.guidance: Candidate should compare CB's device against competitors (Amazon Kindle at 100€, Sony at 120€, Kindle PRO at 150€). CB's device only accepts CB-format books (a disadvantage), but has medium features and 1,000-book storage. The recommended price range is 60–100€ to remain competitive vs. Kindle. The profitability calculation uses a 10€ gross margin per device (e.g., price 70€, cost 60€), though candidates may choose differently within the range.

math.setup: Cost per device = 60€. To compete with Amazon Kindle at 100€, price should be ≤ 100€. A price of 70€ implies a gross margin of 10€/device.
steps: Gross margin per device = price − cost = 70€ − 60€ = 10€
This positions CB below Kindle's 100€ price while acknowledging the format limitation (CB-only)
math.answer: Recommended price: 70€ (or anywhere from 60–100€). Gross margin = price − 60€.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibits 1 and 3, calculate the cannibalization effect: how many CB customers will switch from paper to e-reader, and what is the annual profit impact?
questions.guidance: Use the switching percentages from Exhibit 3 per segment and the reader type mix of CB's 390,000 customers to count switchers. Then calculate the revenue loss from those customers converting their paper purchases to e-book purchases, netting against e-book revenue. The key figure is that switching customers reduce paper book gross margin while gaining e-book gross margin (lower per-book revenue at 8€ vs. 15€).

math.setup: CB total customers: 390,000. Avid (13%) = 50,700; Occasional (18%) = 70,200; Rare (69%) = 269,100. Switch rates: Avid 97% → ~49,179 ≈ use ~50,000 for simplicity per casebook; Occasional 96% → ~67,392; Rare 2.6% → ~6,997. Casebook simplifies: switchers ≈ 50,000 paper-book customers converting. Paper avg 15€ × 33% margin = 4.95€/book lost; e-book avg 8€ × 40% margin = 3.20€/book gained. Net margin loss per book ≈ 1.75€ rounded to 1.8€.
steps: Each switching customer reduces net margin by approximately 1.8€/book
This loss persists every year (no further switching after Year 1 per given data)

questions.prompt: Build the 5-year P&L for the e-book and e-reader business and calculate total profit and payback period.
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply 1% market share to the growing e-book market for annual revenue, apply 40% gross margin, add e-reader device profit (Year 1 high due to switchers buying devices; Year 2+ only new customers from market growth), subtract the one-time website investment, annual general expenses, and annual cannibalization cost.

math.setup: E-book market Year 1 = 48M€, growing 5% annually. CB market share = 1%. E-book gross margin = 40%. E-reader profit: Year 1 = 12,000 devices × 10€ = 120,000€ (11,000 switchers + 1,000 new); Year 2+ ≈ 300-375 new devices × 10€ ≈ 3,000–3,750€. Website investment = −150,000€ (Year 1 only). General expenses = −50,000€/year. Cannibalization = −90,000€/year.
steps: Year 1: Revenue e-books = 48M × 1% = 480,000€; GM = 480,000 × 40% = 192,000€ (casebook shows 190,000€); e-reader profit = 120,000€; website = −150,000€; expenses = −50,000€; cannibalization = −90,000€; Total = ~20,000€
Year 2: Market 50.4M × 1% = 504,000€; GM = 201,600€; e-reader = 3,000€; expenses = −50,000€; cannibalization = −90,000€; Total = ~64,600€
Payback on 150,000€ investment: recovered by end of Year 2 (cumulative profit after Y1+Y2 = 84,600€, break-even mid-Year 2 or early Year 3 depending on timing)
math.answer: 5-year total profit ≈ 342,600€ on a 150,000€ initial investment. Payback period approximately 2–3 years.

brainstorming.prompt: How would you launch this product? (Brainstorming 1) AND What other measures could CB implement to increase revenues? (Brainstorming 2)

categories.name: Launch – Segmentation
ideas: Focus on Avid Readers: highest switching propensity (97%) and highest volume of books consumed
Target existing loyal customers first via in-store promotions before broader launch

categories.name: Launch – Product
ideas: Highlight competitive price vs. Amazon Kindle (if priced at 70–80€)
Emphasize CB's curated non-technical book catalogue as a differentiator
Address the format limitation proactively with exclusive titles or better prices

categories.name: Launch – Price
ideas: Introductory bundle offer: e-reader + X free e-books
Loyalty discounts for existing CB customers
Promotional pricing for Avid Readers to accelerate adoption

categories.name: Launch – Promotion
ideas: In-store promotion at CB physical locations leveraging existing foot traffic
Digital marketing via email to existing customer base
Partner with publishers for exclusive digital content launches

categories.name: Launch – Place
ideas: Sell device exclusively in CB physical stores initially
Expand to CB's new website once launched
Consider pop-up displays in high-traffic areas or partner retail locations

categories.name: Additional Revenue – Products
ideas: Include technical books in the e-book catalogue to attract a broader audience
Expand into audiobooks as a complementary digital product

categories.name: Additional Revenue – Loyalty & Acquisition
ideas: Create a loyalty/points scheme to increase average spending per customer
Launch a referral program to acquire new customers through existing loyal base

categories.name: Additional Revenue – Device & Supplier
ideas: Negotiate with the Chinese manufacturer to add more formats or features, making the device more competitive
Explore white-label arrangements to open the device to other booksellers

recommendation: CB should enter the electronic books market by launching the CB e-Reader and e-book website
Based on projections, the investment generates 342,600€ in cumulative profit over 5 years from a 150,000€ initial investment, with payback in approximately 2–3 years
The e-book market is growing at 5% annually while CB's current paper book segment is stagnant, making this a strategically sound growth avenue
risks: Projections rely on a 1% market share assumption and customer survey data; any deviation in conversion rates or market growth materially affects profitability
Competing chains could enter the e-book market and erode CB's projected share
Cannibalization of existing paper book revenue (estimated 90,000€/year) could be higher if switching rates exceed survey predictions
CB lacks e-commerce experience, which could reduce the quality of customer service — a key value driver for CB's customers (22% cite it as most valued)
Taxes and time value of money were excluded from the analysis; including them would reduce the real profitability of the investment (excellent candidate mention)
next_steps: Conduct a deeper market analysis and further customer surveys to refine market share and switching rate projections
Develop a phased rollout plan targeting Avid Readers first, leveraging in-store channels
Build e-commerce capabilities in-house or partner with a digital platform provider
Explore loyalty programs and referral schemes to protect existing paper book revenue while growing digital
